sections.h2: How large is Coconino County and what does it include?
sections.html:
Coconino County covers 18,661 square miles in north-central Arizona, which makes it the largest county in the state and the second largest in the contiguous United States after San Bernardino County, California. It has more land than nine U.S. states.

Flagstaff is the county seat and the largest city. The county was created in 1891 after residents of the northern part of Yavapai County, tired of traveling to Prescott for county business, petitioned for their own jurisdiction. It takes in Grand Canyon National Park, the Flagstaff metropolitan area, and parts of the Navajo, Hualapai, Hopi, Havasupai and Kaibab reservations, which together account for 7,142 square miles.

One office pair, the Coconino County Assessor and Treasurer, handles property valuation and tax collection across all of it.

sections.h2: What does Coconino County look like in Census numbers?
sections.html:
The 2020 census counted 145,101 people in Coconino County, and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 144,368. The housing count stands out because a quarter of the units were vacant.

Housing units69,108, of which 25.7% vacant2020 census

Renter-occupied share40.8% of occupied units2020 census
Homeowner vacancy rate1.4%2020 census

With about 41 percent of occupied homes rented and a median age of 32.5, Coconino County has a younger, more renter-heavy mix than many Arizona counties, and a quarter of its housing units were vacant on census day. A landlord in Flagstaff or Page selling a rental will want the tax balance, the tenant file and any repair list in hand before a closing.

sections.h2: What drives the Coconino County economy?
sections.html:
Education, health care, a manufacturer, and tourism sit at the top. A 2017 list of the county's largest employers put Northern Arizona University first at 3,500 workers, followed by W. L. Gore and Associates at 3,060 and Flagstaff Medical Center at 2,180, with the Flagstaff Unified School District at 1,590 and Aramark at 1,310.

The Bureau of Economic Analysis counted 87,159 jobs in the county in 2019. Accommodation and food services was the biggest sector at 14,472 jobs, or 16.6 percent, roughly double the national share of 7.5 percent. Health care and social assistance came next at 9,901 jobs, and state government held 8,078, about triple the national share.

For a seller, that mix means house demand and rental demand can follow the university calendar and the visitor season. If a house has been used as a short-term rental, ask the city or county whether any license carries over to a new owner.

sections.h2: How do you get around Coconino County, and why does it matter for a sale?
sections.html:
Flagstaff is a highway junction where Interstate 40 runs east and west and Interstate 17 runs south to Phoenix. U.S. 89 and 180 lead north toward the Grand Canyon.

  • Flagstaff Pulliam Airport, four miles south of downtown, is served by two commercial airlines.
  • Grand Canyon National Park Airport is in Tusayan.
  • Amtrak's Southwest Chief stops in Flagstaff.
  • The Mountain Line runs buses around Flagstaff.
  • The Grand Canyon Railway links Williams with the South Rim.

An owner living in another state can get to Flagstaff by air, which helps with signing and walk-throughs. Parts of the county are reservation land, so ask a title company early about any parcel that might sit on or near it.

sections.h2: Which Coconino County communities and school districts might a seller deal with?
sections.html:
Flagstaff had 65,870 people in the 2010 census, ahead of Sedona at 10,031, Tuba City at 8,611, Page at 7,247 and Williams at 3,023. Fredonia and Tusayan are the county's two incorporated towns.

Sedona sits mostly in Yavapai County, so confirm which county bills a Sedona address before you call an office. The county's K-12 districts are Ash Fork, Flagstaff, Fredonia-Moccasin, Grand Canyon, Page, Sedona-Oak Creek, Tuba City and Williams, plus the Chevelon Butte and Maine Consolidated elementary districts. Two charter schools, Flagstaff Arts and Leadership Academy and Northland Preparatory Academy, also operate here.

Higher education includes Northern Arizona University, Coconino County Community College and a Diné College center in Tuba City.

sections.h2: When do Coconino County property tax payments come due?
sections.html:
Half of the year's tax is due October 1 and half on March 1, and unpaid halves become delinquent after 5:00 p.m. on November 1 and May 1, respectively, under A.R.S. 42-18052. Bills of $100 or less are due in one piece on October 1 and delinquent after December 31 at 5:00 p.m.

The Coconino County Treasurer's office is at 110 E. Cherry Avenue in Flagstaff and keeps hours of 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday. Contact options published on its tax portal:

  • Phone: (928) 679-8188 or (877) 500-1818.
  • Email: treasurer@coconino.az.gov.
  • Automated payment line: 877-884-8060, where you give your tax account or parcel number.
  • Online: enter an account or parcel number in the Treasurer's portal, choose the first half, second half or full payment link, and finish at a third-party payment page.

sections.h2: What does it cost to pay late in Coconino County?
sections.html:
Unpaid tax carries 16 percent simple interest per year after it turns delinquent, with partial months rounded up to whole months (A.R.S. 42-18053). Paying the full year's tax by December 31 of the tax year stops the interest, and interest is not collected where the county's own error caused the delinquency.

An owner who has just paid off a mortgage and then falls behind on taxes can ask for a one-time interest waiver, which needs the county board of supervisors' approval.

sections.h2: How does the lien work if you sell a Coconino County house?
sections.html:
Property tax is a lien on the property that attaches on January 1 of the tax year, and it ranks ahead of nearly all other liens (A.R.S. 42-17153). It stays until the tax is paid in full, until a tax sale purchaser takes title, or until a certificate of removal and abatement issues.

When a Coconino County owner signs a contract, the escrow officer asks the Treasurer for the balance. The amount due, with interest if any, is deducted from the seller's proceeds. A payoff is a standard line on a settlement statement.

sections.h2: How do you challenge a Coconino County valuation?
sections.html:
Start with the assessor's annual notice of value, which Arizona law requires to be mailed before March 1 (A.R.S. 42-15101). Then file a petition for review within 60 days of the mailing date, counting the postmark as the filing date (A.R.S. 42-16051).

The petition needs the owner's opinion of the full cash value and a stated method, such as at least one comparable property or the recent sale of the home. The assessor can amend a notice within 60 days of mailing if a data error affected a group of properties, and after that the roll can change only through the appeal process.

Confirm your own dates with the Assessor's Office, since the notice date can differ by year.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Coconino County property tax?
faqs.a: You can pay online through the Treasurer's portal, by calling the automated line at 877-884-8060, or at the Treasurer's office at 110 E. Cherry Avenue in Flagstaff. Have your account number or parcel number ready.

faqs.q: What are the Coconino County Treasurer's hours?
faqs.a: The Treasurer's tax portal lists hours of 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday. Call (928) 679-8188 or (877) 500-1818 to confirm before you visit.

faqs.q: How much interest applies to late Coconino County taxes?
faqs.a: Delinquent taxes bear 16 percent simple interest per year under Arizona law. Interest is waived if the full year is paid by December 31 or the delinquency was caused by a county error.

faqs.q: Is Coconino County the largest county in Arizona?
faqs.a: Yes. At 18,661 square miles, Coconino County is the largest county in Arizona and the second largest in the contiguous United States.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Coconino County house if the tax bill is unpaid?
faqs.a: Yes. The bill is a lien that has to be paid at closing, and the amount comes out of the seller's proceeds. The title company will get the balance from the Treasurer.
